selection.text: We recorded ear signals from twenty volunteers during a
ninety minute simulated drive. Each volunteer wore a soft
earpiece with four dry electrodes and a reference behind the
ear. The drive was monotonous on purpose, with long straight
roads and very little traffic. Drowsiness was rated by two
observers who watched the face camera without seeing the
signals.

script.text: We recorded ear signals from twenty volunteers during a ninety minute simulated drive.
Each volunteer wore a soft earpiece with four dry electrodes and a reference behind the ear.
The drive was monotonous on purpose, with long straight roads and very little traffic.
Drowsiness was rated by two observers who watched the face camera without seeing the signals.

selection.text: The observers agreed on the drowsiness rating in most of the
one minute windows. Where they disagreed, the difference
was almost always a single step on the rating scale. We used
the mean of the two ratings as the training target for the
detector.

script.text: The observers agreed on the drowsiness rating in most of the one minute windows.
Where they disagreed, the difference was almost always a single step on the rating scale.
We used the mean of the two ratings as the training target for the detector.

selection.text: The detector was trained on one minute windows from
sixteen volunteers. Each window was filtered, cut into short
epochs and summarised by a small set of spectral features. A
gradient boosted classifier then predicted the mean observer
rating for the window.

script.text: The detector was trained on one minute windows from sixteen volunteers.
Each window was filtered, cut into short epochs and summarised by a small set of spectral features.
A gradient boosted classifier then predicted the mean observer rating for the window.

selection.text: Validation used the four remaining volunteers, whose drives
were never seen during training. The predicted ratings agreed
with the observers about as well as the observers agreed with
each other. The largest errors occurred in the first minutes of
each drive, when ratings were low and noisy.

script.text: Fig. 5 shows how the detector is trained and validated.
In panel a, the Recordings come from sixteen volunteers.
The Filtering step removes drift and line noise.
The Features step computes band power in each epoch.
In panel b, the Held-out drive is cut into windows.
The Scoring step compares the prediction with the observers.
Agreement is reported per volunteer.
